variant_or_state: Early V1 / V1 / V2 / V3 bias
known_date_or_corridor: 2000-present; MJM describes flagship since 2000; Effects Database indexes 2003-2008 states and early V1 through V3
relationship_notes: Treat as one family. Effects Database explicitly distinguishes early V1, V1, V2 and V3 bias states; MJM FAQ confirms Germanium, Silicon and bias configurations. Do not equate every color/faceplate with a new generation.
MJM FAQ directly confirms Germanium and explains positive-ground/power behavior; 2017 product description cited in demo material states two hand-matched NOS germanium transistors.
MJM FAQ explicitly confirms Silicon as a separate Fuzz configuration. Exact start/end production dates remain unresolved.

known_date_or_corridor: At least by 2007; later 2017-era and reissue references
relationship_notes: 2007 Effects Database media indexes Low Bias and Mid Bias examples; MJM FAQ confirms bias version; preserve bias as a meaningful configuration rather than a color-only variant.

known_date_or_corridor: Documented by surviving listings by c.2020s; sold as a re-reissue of older hand-painted/stickered London Fuzzes
relationship_notes: Reissue state should remain separate from original production states. Reverb listing says Classic returns to the old design language, uses the same transistor family, and adds an internal bias trimpot.

known_date_or_corridor: By 2013 at latest; historical catalog product
relationship_notes: A 2013 Audiofanzine owner report documents a 2-control version with Fuzz and Volume and describes it as a silicon Fuzz Face-type design. A newer example may add tone; exact revision boundary remains unresolved.

Effects Database published the original two-knob state on 2005-09-19 and describes three hand-selected germaniums with compressed sustain. Treat as the earlier control state, but do not assign a precise retirement date.

Effects Database published the three-knob version on 2005-09-19 and describes a different voicing from the original, with a tone control and three germanium transistors. This is a meaningful identification variant.
Audiofanzine's 2007 owner entry identifies a three-knob analog fuzz and says the enclosure was designed and made in Canada by MJM; multiple sources describe it as Big Muff-derived.

known_date_or_corridor: Documented by 2009-2010; later version differs from catalog image
relationship_notes: 2009 dealer review records two distinct voicings named Leeds and Loose; 2010 Audiofanzine owner report documents a two-knob/toggle version and says a newer version did not match the older photo. Preserve version/graphic evolution for specimen identification.
Catalog spelling varies. Keep both spellings as aliases until primary documentation settles the preferred form.
Reverb identifies a 2010s King Buzz Fuzz and describes it as a three-transistor pedal based on the Burns Buzzaround; older dealer copy describes NOS germanium and positive-ground operation.
Zikinf records Phantom as no longer manufactured and explicitly links it with Blues Devil and Luxora as three MJM overdrive variants/states; Equipboard links Luxora as the newer option.

variant_or_state: Early handmade state; specimen dated 2002 by owner report
relationship_notes: Audiofanzine owner report identifies an analog handmade overdrive made in Canada and dates the reviewed pedal to 2002. The report mentions component-type changes in later examples; archive should not turn that anecdote into a universal production boundary.

known_date_or_corridor: Later than Phantom; exact first date unresolved
relationship_notes: Equipboard explicitly presents Luxora as a newer option to the discontinued Phantom, while Zikinf lists it as the third MJM overdrive alongside Blues Devil and Phantom. Preserve relationship as evidence-qualified, not an exact generational date.
